brief: Deutsche Bank raises Meta's price target to $820 from $750 (25x FY27 EPS, up from 23x) after attending the Muse Connect keynote and demoing new devices. Muse, Meta's AI agent, became the #1 iOS Productivity app (4.9 stars, 38k ratings) and drove over 3mn US installs in 16 days, versus ChatGPT's 35 days to match that pace. Free users get up to 100mn tokens weekly; Power ($20/mo) and Maximum ($100/mo) tiers show little upgrade incentive yet, so DB reads this as a user-acquisition phase ahead of monetization. Early partnerships (Walmart, Best Buy, Instacart, Shopify, Expedia, others) likely carry no revenue share yet, giving integrated merchants free traffic. Amazon still blocks Muse, but DB expects it could eventually lift that block, especially as Walmart's deal raises Amazon's cost of staying outside. New hardware, translating Glasses, audio Glasses, $1,299 VR Glasses due Spring 2027, and the holiday-bound Muse Charm, broadens distribution. DB models Muse at roughly mid-single-digit percent of 2030 Meta revenue, high-single-digit upside, which it calls conservative, against $25-50 per user in VM capex. Separately, DB flags agent-driven disintermediation risk across travel, e-commerce and subscription services, with Airbnb, Chewy and music-streaming DSPs seen as relatively insulated.
